Chooses how this texture combines with what lies below it. A texture on layer 0 blends with the surface itself, a texture on layer 1 blends with layer 0, and so on up to layer 7. Layers are set with the index argument of [EntityTexture](EntityTexture) or [BrushTexture](BrushTexture).

| Blend | Result |
|---|---|
| 0 | No blending. |
| 1 | Alpha: uses the alpha of the texture. |
| 2 | Multiply, the default. |
| 3 | Add. |
| 4 | Dot3 bump mapping. |
| 5 | Multiply twice as bright (x2). |

```blitzbasic
;media still textures/textureblend.png
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
CameraClsColor camera, 70, 100, 160
light = CreateLight()
RotateEntity light, 40, 30, 0

base = CreateTexture(64, 64, 1 + 4096)
SetBuffer TextureBuffer(base)
ClsColor 230, 200, 120
Cls
Color 160, 120, 40
For i = 0 To 63 Step 16
	Rect 0, i, 64, 8, 1
Next
over = CreateTexture(64, 64, 1 + 4096)
SetBuffer TextureBuffer(over)
ClsColor 60, 60, 60
Cls
Color 255, 255, 255
Oval 8, 8, 48, 48, 1
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
TextureBlend over, 3

cube = CreateCube() : PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 4.4 : TurnEntity cube, 25, 35, 0
EntityTexture cube, base, 0, 0
EntityTexture cube, over, 0, 1
RenderWorld
Flip
WaitKey
```

![TextureBlend](media/textures/textureblend.png)
@param texture  The texture to change.
@param blend    Blend mode from the table above.
@gap Layers that have no texture or a blend of 0 are left out, and the layers after them move up, so the first of the others is blended with the surface like the original does. Dot3 on a layer after the first one is the dot product of the texture and what the layers before it made, which needs a GPU that can read the target while it draws to it (the ones that support Dither 2); other GPUs and a Graphics with AntiAlias multiply instead.
